# Worker Registry


## Browsing the registry

The iii Worker Registry at [workers.iii.dev](https://workers.iii.dev/) is the index of installable
workers. Each worker page lists the trigger types and functions it provides, its configuration
schema, supported platforms, and agent skills. Use that information to locate a worker that fulfills
a capability your project needs.

{/* TODO: Add a llm-only note here on how an llm can browse the registry once that surface is stable in the skills worker */}

## Adding a worker

`compose::add` adds a registry worker to the running project. Compose writes the worker and its
registry dependencies to `worker-compose.yaml` and starts them. Workers that did not change continue
to run.

```bash
iii trigger compose::add worker=state
```

<Note>
  If the Compose daemon runs in a namespace other than `default`, add `-n <namespace>`. For version
  selectors and the full steps, see [Add a registry worker](./workers#add-a-registry-worker). To add
  a worker from a local directory, see [Adding workers](./compose#adding-workers). For the settings
  of each worker, see [Configuration](./configuration). To check status, update, or remove a worker,
  see [Workers](./workers) and [Compose](./compose).
</Note>

## Artifact types

Compose runs `binary` registry workers as processes on the host and `bundle` registry workers in a
VM. Compose rejects `engine` and `image` registry workers. `engine` workers ship with the engine.
`image` workers need an OCI runtime. For platform limits, see
[Worker kinds](./compose#worker-kinds).
